items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I’ve never been to Russia, but Benny Goodman went to Russia.

ctx.x: Well some people have mentioned that when they’ve gone to Europe and the Europeans say to them, you know, your country is very young. And in a way I think some of our problems stem from that, is that we have a ways to go.

You know you can put the greatest marquee together of the greatest jazz stars in this country. And maybe, maybe you’ll get a thousand people. Maybe. Not for sure. You go to Japan, you go to Europe, with that same card, and you’ll have fifty thousand people. Or twenty thousand people. Vastly more than here. People aren’t interested in jazz here, except the few that understand and appreciate it and realize its meaning. And it’s not that difficult to understand. People say they don’t understand it. What’s there to…
or classic music. The musicians made more than the doctors or engineers did. That’s how they appreciated it. But maybe not so now I don’t know. Anyway.
